tiers.name: Prohibited AI violations
tiers.trigger_summary: Use of any AI practice prohibited under Article 5 (subliminal manipulation, exploitation of vulnerabilities, social scoring by public authorities, predictive policing by profiling alone, untargeted facial scraping, emotion recognition in workplace or education with limited exceptions, biometric categorisation on sensitive attributes, real-time remote biometric identification in public spaces with narrow law-enforcement exceptions)
tiers.applies_to: providers, importers, distributors, deployers, and any other operator

tiers.name: Other violations of the Act, including Article 50 transparency and high-risk obligations
tiers.trigger_summary: Non-compliance with provider obligations, importer obligations, distributor obligations, deployer obligations under Article 26, notified body obligations, or transparency obligations under Article 50

tiers.name: Misleading information to authorities
tiers.trigger_summary: Supplying incorrect, incomplete, or misleading information to notified bodies or national competent authorities in reply to a request

sme_treatment.rule: For SMEs, including start-ups, each fine referred to in this Article shall be up to the percentages or amount referred to in paragraphs 3, 4, and 5, whichever is lower.
sme_treatment.practical_meaning: SMEs face the LOWER of the absolute amount and the turnover percentage, not the higher. This is the inverse of the rule that applies to larger companies.

factors_considered_article_99_7: Nature, gravity, and duration of the infringement and of its consequences
Whether administrative fines have already been applied by other authorities for the same infringement
Size, annual turnover, and market share of the operator
Other aggravating or mitigating factors applicable to the circumstances
Degree of cooperation with national competent authorities
Degree of responsibility of the operator, taking technical and organisational measures into account
Manner in which the infringement became known to the national competent authorities (especially whether the operator notified)
Intentional or negligent character of the infringement
Adherence to approved codes of conduct or certification mechanisms
enforcement_authority: Each EU Member State designates a national competent authority. Penalties are imposed at Member State level under Member State procedural rules.
note: These are maximum bounds set by the Regulation. Actual fines imposed will be calibrated against the Article 99(7) factors and Member State practice. Read alongside Article 99 in full for the procedural detail.
